definition: Vilify means to attack someone's reputation with cruel or unjust words.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word vilify. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know vilify should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: When the factory closed, its former owner used every interview to vilify the union, blaming the very workers who had taken pay cuts to keep the doors open.
Criticism can be fair and even friendly; it stops far short of vilifying, which sets out to blacken the person rather than weigh the work.
Demonize goes further than vilify: the vilified man is made to look worthless, while the demonized one is made to look like evil itself.

Malign means to speak harmful, usually unfair words about someone, and it stays small and scattered — a resentful aside here, a whisper passed along there. Vilify is bigger and louder: a sustained public campaign to make its target look worthless. Being maligned stings; being vilified can ruin a name.

Smear means to spread a damaging accusation — true or invented — and ride it; it is journalism's word for a campaign built on charges. Vilify aims wider than any one accusation: it attacks the whole character. A smear pins a charge on you; to vilify is to blacken the man himself.

Defame is the legal term for injuring a reputation with false statements — the word of courtrooms, lawsuits, and damages. Vilify describes the cruelty of the attack, not its legal standing: you can vilify someone viciously without ever being sued. Defamation is an offense; vilifying is an act.
